headline: Australia Doubles Renewable Energy Capacity in Record Year
meta_description: Australia connected 9.1 GW of solar, wind and battery capacity in 2025/26, more than double the previous year, with 2.7 GW of battery storage added.
summary_short: Australia achieved a landmark renewable energy milestone, connecting record new capacity to its grid as battery storage accelerates the clean energy transition.
body:
Australia connected a record 9.1 gigawatts of new solar, wind and battery capacity to its grid during the 2025/26 financial year—more than double the capacity added in the year before.

The surge reflects a dramatic acceleration in the country's energy transition. Battery storage proved particularly crucial, with 2.7 gigawatts of battery capacity added during the same period, enabling the grid to store and manage renewable power more effectively.

This growth underscores how rapidly renewable infrastructure is scaling across Australia. The doubling of annual capacity additions suggests momentum is building toward a cleaner, more resilient energy system—one that increasingly relies on wind, solar and storage rather than fossil fuels.
quick_facts: 9.1 GW of renewable capacity connected in 2025/26 financial year
More than double the previous year's additions
2.7 GW of battery storage added in same period
Australia's grid increasingly powered by solar, wind and batteries
